---
title: "A GEPA learning journey"
description: >
  Run a deterministic, offline GEPA search with separate training,
  validation and holdout data, then inspect feedback, lineage and budget.
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{A GEPA learning journey}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

GEPA improves instructions by scoring candidate programs, showing a reflection
model the failures, and asking it to rewrite the instructions. This journey
uses a small support-ticket task and an offline Chat fixture so the complete
path runs in documentation builds without credentials.

The fixture is deliberately scripted to make each transition predictable. Its
scores show that the workflow, feedback, result fields and budget accounting
work; they are not evidence that a real model improves. A live-model example
and the checkpoint limits appear below.

## Define the task and data splits

Route tickets as `urgent` when they report a current outage or compromised
account, and `routine` otherwise. Keep the three data sets separate: GEPA sees
training rows when it gathers failures for reflection, validation rows when it
selects candidates, and holdout rows only for the final comparison.

```{r task-data}
library(dsprrr)

train <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "Checkout is unavailable for every customer during an outage.",
    "Please update the billing contact.",
    "An unknown user took over my account.",
    "When is the next invoice due?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "routine", "urgent", "routine")
)

validation <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "A production outage is blocking every customer.",
    "A stranger gained access to my account.",
    "Can I change my billing email?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "urgent", "routine")
)

holdout <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "A service outage is stopping password resets.",
    "An attacker accessed my account overnight.",
    "Please add a second billing contact.",
    "Where can I see next month's invoice?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "urgent", "routine", "routine")
)

program <- module(signature(
  "ticket -> severity: enum('urgent', 'routine')",
  instructions = "Use a quick baseline rule."
))
```

The fixture implements the small part of ellmer's Chat protocol used here. It
returns a routine label for the baseline, an outage-only proposal on its first
reflection, and a complete rule after it sees feedback about the missed
account-compromise case. It is only an offline teaching fixture; use an
ellmer Chat constructor such as `ellmer::chat_openai()` in an application.

```{r fixture-chat}
fixture_chat_class <- R6::R6Class(
  "Chat",
  public = list(
    turns = NULL,
    initialize = function(model, responder) {
      self$turns <- list()
      private$model <- ellmer::Model(name = model, extra_args = list())
      private$provider <- ellmer::Provider(name = "fixture", base_url = "")
      private$responder <- responder
    },
    chat = function(prompt, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), NULL, ...)
    },
    chat_structured = function(prompt, type, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), type, ...)
    },
    stream = function(...) character(),
    get_turns = function() self$turns,
    set_turns = function(turns) {
      self$turns <- turns
      invisible(self)
    },
    last_turn = function(role = NULL) NULL,
    get_model = function() private$model@name,
    get_provider = function() private$provider,
    get_model_object = function() private$model
  ),
  private = list(model = NULL, provider = NULL, responder = NULL),
  lock_objects = FALSE,
  parent_env = globalenv()
)

new_fixture_chat <- function(model, responder) {
  audit <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  audit$prompts <- character()
  wrapped_responder <- function(prompt, type, ...) {
    prompt <- paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n")
    audit$prompts <- c(audit$prompts, prompt)
    responder(prompt, type, ...)
  }
  list(
    chat = fixture_chat_class$new(model, wrapped_responder),
    audit = audit
  )
}

partial_rule <- paste(
  "Mark a ticket urgent when it reports an explicit outage;",
  "otherwise mark it routine."
)
complete_rule <- paste(
  "Mark tickets urgent when they report a current service outage",
  "or compromised account; otherwise mark them routine."
)

task_fixture <- new_fixture_chat("fixture-task", function(prompt, type, ...) {
  prompt_lines <- strsplit(prompt, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  input_header <- grep("^# Input:", prompt_lines)
  ticket_line <- grep("^ticket: ", prompt_lines, value = TRUE)
  if (length(input_header) != 1L || length(ticket_line) != 1L) {
    stop("Task fixture could not read one ticket from the prompt")
  }

  instructions <- paste(
    prompt_lines[seq_len(input_header - 1L)],
    collapse = "\n"
  )
  ticket <- sub("^ticket: ", "", ticket_line[[1L]])
  outage_rule <- grepl("explicit outage", instructions, fixed = TRUE) ||
    grepl("current service outage", instructions, fixed = TRUE)
  compromise_rule <- grepl("compromised account", instructions, fixed = TRUE)
  outage <- grepl(
    "outage|unavailable|blocking|stopping|down",
    ticket,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  compromised <- grepl(
    "unknown user|stranger gained access|attacker|unknown login|compromised",
    ticket,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  urgent <- (outage_rule && outage) || (compromise_rule && compromised)
  list(severity = if (urgent) "urgent" else "routine")
})

reflection_fixture <- new_fixture_chat(
  "fixture-reflection",
  function(prompt, type, ...) {
    account_failure <- grepl(
      "Expected urgent but got routine",
      prompt,
      fixed = TRUE
    ) && grepl(
      "An unknown user took over my account.",
      prompt,
      fixed = TRUE
    )
    instructions <- if (account_failure) {
      complete_rule
    } else {
      partial_rule
    }
    list(instructions = instructions)
  }
)

old_cache <- configure_cache(enable = FALSE)
```

## Score the baseline

The metric returns both a score and a sentence the reflection step can use.
The baseline fixture intentionally misses both urgent validation rows.

```{r feedback-and-baseline}
feedback_metric <- metric_with_feedback(
  function(prediction, expected) {
    correct <- identical(prediction$severity, expected$severity)
    list(
      score = as.numeric(correct),
      feedback = if (correct) {
        "Correct."
      } else {
        paste0(
          "Expected ", expected$severity, " but got ",
          prediction$severity,
          ". Check for an outage or a compromised account."
        )
      }
    )
  },
  field = "severity"
)

baseline_validation <- evaluate(
  program,
  validation,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)

baseline_validation$mean_score
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(baseline_validation$mean_score), 1 / 3)))

data.frame(
  ticket = validation$ticket,
  expected = validation$severity,
  predicted = vapply(
    baseline_validation$predictions,
    `[[`,
    character(1),
    "severity"
  ),
  score = baseline_validation$scores
)
```

## Run a bounded search

`.llm` evaluates candidate instructions. `.reflection_llm` proposes new
instructions from training failures and their feedback. The two roles can use
different models; this fixture keeps them local and deterministic. The
`optimizer_control()` cap applies to the compile run.

```{r compile-gepa}
task_prompt_start <- length(task_fixture$audit$prompts)
reflection_prompt_start <- length(reflection_fixture$audit$prompts)

optimized <- compile(
  program,
  GEPA(
    metric = feedback_metric,
    population_size = 2L,
    generations = 2L,
    mutation_rate = 1,
    crossover_rate = 0,
    selection = "current_best",
    seed = 42L,
    verbose = FALSE
  ),
  train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .reflection_llm = reflection_fixture$chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 40L,
    progress = FALSE
  )
)

result <- optimization_result(optimized)
result
```

The first proposal handles outages but still misses compromised accounts. The
next reflection sees the failed training row and its feedback:

```{r reflection-feedback}
optimizer_task_prompts <- task_fixture$audit$prompts[
  seq.int(task_prompt_start + 1L, length(task_fixture$audit$prompts))
]
optimizer_reflection_prompts <- reflection_fixture$audit$prompts[
  seq.int(reflection_prompt_start + 1L, length(reflection_fixture$audit$prompts))
]

feedback_prompts <- optimizer_reflection_prompts[
  grepl("Feedback:", optimizer_reflection_prompts, fixed = TRUE)
]
stopifnot(
  length(feedback_prompts) > 0L,
  grepl(
    "Expected urgent but got routine",
    feedback_prompts[[1L]],
    fixed = TRUE
  ),
  grepl(train$ticket[[3L]], feedback_prompts[[1L]], fixed = TRUE)
)
feedback_lines <- strsplit(feedback_prompts[[1L]], "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
cat(grep("Feedback:", feedback_lines, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")

optimizer_prompts <- paste(
  c(optimizer_task_prompts, optimizer_reflection_prompts),
  collapse = "\n"
)
stopifnot(
  !any(vapply(
    holdout$ticket,
    grepl,
    logical(1),
    x = optimizer_prompts,
    fixed = TRUE
  ))
)
```

The prompt audit confirms that holdout tickets did not enter candidate
evaluation or reflection. They are only used after the search. The result's
GEPA extension records each candidate's parent and validation score:

```{r candidate-lineage}
gepa_details <- result$extensions$gepa
candidate_ids <- names(gepa_details$candidates)

candidate_lineage <- data.frame(
  candidate_id = candidate_ids,
  parent = vapply(candidate_ids, function(candidate_id) {
    parents <- gepa_details$parents[[candidate_id]]
    if (length(parents) == 0L) "seed" else paste(parents, collapse = ", ")
  }, character(1)),
  validation_score = unname(gepa_details$val_aggregate_scores[candidate_ids]),
  selected = candidate_ids == result$lineage$best_candidate_id
)
candidate_lineage
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(any(candidate_lineage$selected)),
  isTRUE(result$best_score == 1),
  isTRUE(candidate_lineage$validation_score[
    candidate_lineage$selected
  ] == 1)
)

list(
  candidate_id = result$lineage$best_candidate_id,
  validation_score = result$best_score,
  instructions = result$best_params$component_values[[1L]]$value
)
```

## Compare once on holdout

The holdout comparison is a separate `evaluate()` call. It does not change
GEPA's candidate selection or its recorded budget.

```{r heldout-comparison}
holdout_before <- evaluate(
  program,
  holdout,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)
holdout_after <- evaluate(
  optimized,
  holdout,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  ticket = holdout$ticket,
  expected = holdout$severity,
  before = vapply(holdout_before$predictions, `[[`, character(1), "severity"),
  after = vapply(holdout_after$predictions, `[[`, character(1), "severity")
)

c(
  before = holdout_before$mean_score,
  after = holdout_after$mean_score
)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(holdout_before$mean_score == 0.5),
  isTRUE(holdout_after$mean_score == 1)
)
```

The fixture score rises from 0.5 to 1.0 on these four holdout rows. This is a
scripted workflow demonstration, not a real-model improvement claim. Candidate
selection, feedback and results from a live search are stochastic and may not
follow this path.

## Read the budget and choose objectives

The public [optimization result](../reference/optimization_result.html) gives
the compile budget and its configured limits. Here, the GEPA search used 28
metric calls from its 40-call cap. The baseline validation and two holdout
evaluations below are outside that compile budget:

```{r budget-summary}
gepa_budget <- result$budget
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$metric_calls == 28),
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$metric_calls <= gepa_budget$limits$max_metric_calls)
)
metric_accounting <- data.frame(
  phase = c(
    "GEPA compile",
    "Baseline validation",
    "Before and after holdout evaluations"
  ),
  metric_calls = c(
    gepa_budget$metric_calls,
    nrow(validation),
    2L * nrow(holdout)
  )
)
metric_accounting <- rbind(
  metric_accounting,
  data.frame(
    phase = "Total across this article",
    metric_calls = sum(metric_accounting$metric_calls)
  )
)
metric_accounting
stopifnot(isTRUE(metric_accounting$metric_calls[[4L]] == 39))

gepa_budget$limits$max_metric_calls
```

This example has one objective, so candidates are ranked by that score. With
several named metrics and the default `selection = "pareto"`, GEPA ranks
non-dominated trade-offs across objectives; it does not reduce them to one
weighted score. `selection = "current_best"` instead ranks candidates only by
the first metric.

The fixture does not report provider token counts or cost. With real Chats, use
`optimizer_control(max_provider_calls = ..., max_total_tokens = ..., max_cost
= ...)` to limit provider usage when the provider supplies the required
measurements. Finite limits are checked between metric rows and optimizer
provider calls, so the last row or call can overshoot a limit; a cost limit is
not a hard provider-side spending ceiling. If a provider does not report a
value, a finite cap cannot be enforced by guessing.

## Where GEPA fits

- **GEPA** searches candidate instructions from task failures and feedback.
- **Flex** lets GEPA change a complete program source; it is a separate
  experimental path described in [Flex: optimize a whole program](flex-optimization.html).
- **Omni** compares several optimizers from the same starting program and can
  continue from the selected result; see [Compose optimizers with Omni](omni-meta-optimization.html).
- **AutoResearch** and **MetaHarness** are outer experiment harnesses: an
  agent proposes edits, and dsprrr's R evaluator validates and scores them.
  See [Agentic optimization harnesses](agentic-optimization-harnesses.html).

In DSPy 3.5.0, GEPA uses a native search budget chosen as exactly one of
`auto`, `max_full_evals` or `max_metric_calls`, and its feedback metric can
receive predictor and execution-trace context. dsprrr's `GEPA()` exposes
`population_size` and `generations`, with optional call, token, cost and time
limits through `optimizer_control()`; `metric_with_feedback()` receives the
prediction and expected row. Similar names do not make candidate paths or
scores interchangeable. See the [DSPy 3.5.0 GEPA source](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/3.5.0/dspy/teleprompt/gepa/gepa.py).

## Checkpoints and an opt-in live run

GEPA checkpoint resume supports sequential `round_robin` searches over plain
`Predict` leaves and built-in predictor pipelines that return plain data. It
does not support Flex, other component selectors, custom module types or
custom Chats, Chats with tools, or Chats with existing turns. A resume must
match the original program, data, metrics, algorithm settings and effective
Chat identities; resource limits may change. Completed proposals and
evaluation rows are restored, but a provider request interrupted after the
provider completes and before the result is committed may run again after a
crash. Resume does not guarantee exactly-once provider effects. See the
[GEPA reference](../reference/GEPA.html) for the full contract.

To try a live search with your own labeled data, create separate task and
reflection Chats and set a budget. This block is opt-in and is not run during
documentation builds:

```{r live-gepa, eval=FALSE}
task_chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna")
reflection_chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-astra")

live_result <- compile(
  program,
  GEPA(
    metric = feedback_metric,
    population_size = 6L,
    generations = 3L,
    seed = 42L
  ),
  train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = task_chat,
  .reflection_llm = reflection_chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 80L,
    max_provider_calls = 50L,
    max_cost = 1
  )
)

optimization_result(live_result)
```

If `.reflection_llm` is omitted, an explicitly supplied `.llm` is also used
for reflection as a compatibility fallback. The reflection model proposes
instructions; the task model scores them. Compare models with the same data,
validation set, seed and limits, and inspect `optimization_result()` rather
than treating a fixture score or one stochastic run as a general result.

```{r restore-cache, include=FALSE}
if (is.null(old_cache)) {
  configure_cache(enable = TRUE)
} else {
  do.call(configure_cache, old_cache)
}
```
